importantNotes: Acts 1:8 is the outline of the book: Jerusalem → Judea/Samaria → ends of the earth.
Pentecost (ch. 2) marks the birthday of the church — the Spirit comes in power.
Paul's three missionary journeys are the backbone of the second half of Acts.
The Bereans (17:11) are commended for examining Scripture daily — a model for all believers.
Acts has no formal ending — suggesting the church's mission continues today.

chapters.1: Jesus ascends to heaven; the apostles pray and choose Matthias to replace Judas.
chapters.2: The Holy Spirit comes at Pentecost; Peter preaches; 3,000 are saved; the church begins.
chapters.3: Peter heals a lame man at the Temple gate; preaches about Jesus to the crowd.
chapters.4: Peter and John arrested; they boldly proclaim Christ; the believers share everything.
chapters.5: Ananias and Sapphira die for lying; the apostles perform miracles and are arrested.
chapters.6: Seven deacons appointed; Stephen, full of grace and power, is accused of blasphemy.
chapters.7: Stephen's defense — a history of Israel; he is stoned to death as the first Christian martyr.
chapters.8: Persecution scatters the church; Philip in Samaria; the Ethiopian eunuch is baptized.
chapters.9: Saul's conversion on the road to Damascus; he begins preaching that Jesus is the Christ.
chapters.10: Peter's vision of the sheet; Cornelius and his household receive the Gospel and the Holy Spirit.
chapters.11: Peter explains the Gentile conversion to the Jerusalem church; the church at Antioch grows.
chapters.12: James is executed; Peter is imprisoned and miraculously freed by an angel; Herod dies.
chapters.13: Paul and Barnabas sent on the first missionary journey; preaching in Cyprus and Antioch.
chapters.14: Ministry in Iconium, Lystra, and Derbe; Paul is stoned but survives; churches established.
chapters.15: The Jerusalem Council — Gentiles do not need circumcision; the gospel is for all.
chapters.16: Paul's second journey; Timothy joins; the Macedonian call; Lydia converted; the Philippian jailer.
chapters.17: Paul in Thessalonica and Berea; his sermon on Mars Hill in Athens — the unknown God.
chapters.18: Paul in Corinth for 18 months; Aquila and Priscilla; Apollos begins preaching.
chapters.19: Paul in Ephesus — extraordinary miracles; the riot of the silversmiths.
chapters.20: Paul travels through Macedonia and Greece; Eutychus raised; farewell to the Ephesian elders.
chapters.21: Paul returns to Jerusalem despite warnings; he is arrested in the Temple.
chapters.22: Paul's defense before the crowd — his testimony of conversion.
chapters.23: Paul before the Sanhedrin; a plot to kill him; he is transferred to Caesarea.
chapters.24: Paul's trial before Governor Felix — he speaks about faith in Christ.
chapters.25: Paul appeals to Caesar before Festus; King Agrippa hears the case.
chapters.26: Paul's defense before Agrippa — 'I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision.'
chapters.27: Paul's voyage to Rome; a shipwreck on the way; all 276 passengers survive.
chapters.28: Paul arrives in Rome; he preaches the kingdom of God under house arrest.
